text: Order Recombination (OR/OX): Worked Example (7 genes) Parents (permutations, length 7): P1 = [A B C D E F G], P2 = [C F A G D B E ] Goal: build a valid child permutation that preserves relative order from P2 while inheriting a block from P1. 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 P1 : A B C D E F GC D E P2 : C F A G D B E We will choose cut points at positions 3..5 and copy that block from P1. 9 / 27 OR/OX Step 1: Choose cut points and copy the block from P1 Cut points: positions 3..5. Copy P1[3..5] = [C D E ] into the child at the same positions. Child: C D E cut cut Now the child has a fixed block; the remaining positions must be filled using the relative order of cities as they appear in P2 (skipping duplicates). 10 / 27 OR/OX Step 2: Scan P2 cyclically and skip duplicates Rule: start scanning P2 after the second cut point (after position 5), wrap around, and list cities not yet in the child. P2 : C F A G D B E start scan after cut C D EF A G B Fill list (scan order):[B, F , A, G] Scan order: B → E → C → F → A → G → D Skip {C , D, E } (already copied). Keep the rest in that order. 11 / 27 OR/OX Step 3: Insert the fill list into empty slots (cyclically) Empty slots in the child: positions 1, 2, 6, 7. Insertion rule: start filling after the second cut point (positions 6, 7, 1, 2). Child slots: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 C D E Fill list: [B, F , A, G] B FA G Insert after the cut: positions 6 → 7 → 1 → 2 So B goes to pos6, F to pos7, A to pos1, G to pos2. 12 / 27 OR/OX Result: Final Child and What Was Preserved Final child COR/OX = [A G C D E B F ] What was preserved? ▶ The block [C D E ] is copied exactly from P1. ▶ The remaining genes [B, F , A, G] appear in the child in the same relative order as in the cyclic scan of P2. Note OR/OX preserves a contiguous block from one parent and the relative order from the other. Child A G C D E B FC D EA G B F Gray = copied block from P1 Green = filled from P2 order 13 / 27
